docs.title: aibi-toolkit
docs.text:
CLI + library for cleaning up Power BI / Tableau semantic-model metadata.

pip install aibi-toolkit
aibi --help
Command Purpose summary object counts tables list table names audit hygiene findings + score lint DAX rule findings export measures to CSV diagram mermaid ER diagram fix naming/format auto-fixes report markdown audit report synth demo model generator

docs.title: Using the toolkit
docs.text:
Start with the quick audit example in the repo, or dive into the pages below for each command family:

  • Input formats — JSON dumps vs .pbip TMDL folders
  • Naming and format strings
  • Auditing and linting
  • Tables for the table listing and follow-ups
  • Autofixes and profiling
  • Diagrams and the CLI reference

Current status: v1.3.0 (2026-11-18) — TMDL/PBIP folder input, every command exposed via --json, refreshed CLI reference, TMDL page, and the write-failure hardening passed for docs/.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Every command takes a model path first. A model path may be either:

  • a shared-schema JSON dump (model.json produced by your model tool), or
  • a .pbip-style TMDL directory — a project root, a *.Dataset folder, or a bare definition/ directory. definition/tables/*.tmdl feeds the table list; definition/relationships.tmdl feeds the relationship checks.

Output-oriented commands (export, report, lint, fix, profile, summary, tables, audit, diagram) are described here. synth generates a sample model instead of reading one.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
$ aibi summary model.json
tables=4 measures=8 columns=4

$ aibi summary model.json --json
{"tables": 4, "measures": 8, "columns": 4}

Prints one line: tables=N measures=N columns=N. tables counts table objects; measures counts measure objects; columns counts columns in table objects. --json prints the same data as {"tables": 4, "measures": 8, "columns": 4}.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — model loaded, line printed.
  • 2 — model path missing, non-JSON, or top-level shape not an object.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
$ aibi tables model.json
Sales
Customer
Product
Date

$ aibi tables model.json --json
["Sales", "Customer", "Product", "Date"]

One table name per line, in persisted order. --json prints ["Sales", "Customer", "Product", "Date"] (a JSON array, in the same order).

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — model loaded, list printed.
  • 2 — model path missing, non-JSON, or top-level shape not an object.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
$ aibi audit model.json
[missing_format] Measure 1
[duplicate_names] Measure 1
score=38

Findings are [category] measure name, one per line, then score=N/100 at the bottom. Categories: missing_format (no formatString), duplicate_names (case-insensitive duplicate measure names), long_names (over 64 chars).

--json prints {"score": 38, "findings": {category: [names]}} instead of the text output — same content, easier to parse in CI.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 1 — at least one finding.
  • 0 — model loaded and clean (score is not printed in that case; only no findings would appear, currently it does — check empty output).

docs.title: Lint
docs.text:
$ aibi lint model.json
[lint] Measure name: use DIVIDE instead of / to guard divide-by-zero

aibi lint is the DAX-oriented static check. Findings are [lint] measure name: <reason>. No output means the sample passed every check — return code is then 0.

--json prints {"lint": {measure_name: [reasons]}} for machine reading. --list-rules prints the rule inventory (name and rewrite message) and exits 0 without reading a model; --list-rules --json emits [{"name": ..., "message": ...}].

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 1 — at least one finding.
  • 0 — no findings.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
$ aibi fix model.json
fixed: measure 'Measure 1' -> 'Measure'
fixed: format for 'Measure' -> $#,0.00

Normalises what the audit would flag — names (snake_case/kebab/collapse), format strings, extras in the dump. --dry-run prints each proposed fix without touching anything.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — fixes were proposed (or applied when --dry-run is omitted; same count).
  • 1 — nothing to fix.
  • 2 — model path missing.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
$ aibi profile model.json
count=8 avg=0.0 max=0

Expression-complexity profile. count / avg / max are counts of DAX weight; heavier measures matter more in review. --json exposes {"count": N, "avg": N, "max": N, "heavy": [names]} for tooling.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — model loaded.
  • 2 — model path missing.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
$ aibi export model.json out.csv
exported 8 measures to out.csv

Writes CSV with columns table,name,expression,formatString. Unwrapped measure rows carry their enclosing table in the left column.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — CSV written.
  • 2 — model path missing, or output path unwritable. One-line reason on stderr; never a traceback.

docs.title: Report
docs.text:
$ aibi report model.json out.md
report written to out.md

Markdown report: # Model Audit Report, score, tables/measures, measure findings, table findings (empty tables, bad names), relationship findings (inactive, bidirectional, missing cardinality), plus an appendix of rules.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — report written.
  • 2 — model path missing, or output path unwritable. One-line reason on stderr; never a traceback.

docs.title: Diagram
docs.text:
$ aibi diagram model.json
erDiagram
    Sales ||--o{ Customer : has
    Sales ||--o{ Product : has

Writes a mermaid erDiagram to stdout. Paste it into a mermaid-rendered markdown document or view in the mermaid CLI.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — diagram printed.
  • 2 — model path missing.

docs.title: Synth
docs.text:
$ aibi synth out.json
sample model written to out.json

Writes a small model.json suitable as scaffolding, or as a feed for the other commands. Tables seeded: Sales, Customer, Product, Date with two measures each. --tables N overrides the table count.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — file written.
  • 2 — file path unwritable.

docs.title: Explain
docs.text:
$ aibi explain double_negation
double_negation
NOT(NOT(x)) is just x — drop the double wrapper
pattern: (?:\bNOT\s*\(|!)\s*(?:\bNOT\s*\(|!)

With no rule name, aibi explain prints the same inventory as --list-rules and exits 0. --json prints {"name", "pattern", "message"} for one rule, or an array for the inventory. Names are case-insensitive; an unknown name exits 2 with the inventory on stderr.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — rule found (or no name given).
  • 2 — unknown rule name.

docs.title: Every command at a glance
docs.text: Command Reads model Writes Exit codes summary yes stdout 0 / 2 tables yes stdout 0 / 2 audit yes stdout 0 / 1 / 2 lint yes stdout 0 / 1 / 2 fix yes stdout / model 0 / 1 / 2 profile yes stdout 0 / 2 diagram yes stdout 0 / 2 export yes CSV 0 / 2 report yes markdown 0 / 2 synth no JSON 0 / 2 explain no stdout 0 / 2

docs.title: Exit codes (global)
docs.text:
• 0 — the command produced its output (or clean run).
  • 1 — findings exist on an audit/lint-style command.
  • 2 — usage error. Missing path, non-JSON, wrong top-level shape, or an unwritable output path — always one line on stderr, never a traceback.

Every command supports --help.

docs.title: Auditing
docs.text:
aibi audit model.json

Exits non-zero when findings exist, so it works as a CI gate:

- run: aibi audit model.json

docs.title: Score
docs.text: The 0-100 score penalizes missing formats (heaviest), duplicate names, and overly long names.

docs.title: Relationship checks
docs.text: integrity.check_relationships flags inactive and bidirectional relationships; check_cardinality flags missing cardinality.

docs.title: Auto-fixes
docs.text:
aibi fix model.json          # prints fixes and the updated model JSON
aibi fix --dry-run model.json  # prints fixes only

Fixes are naming normalizations and format-string suggestions. Review the change log before applying to a real model.

docs.title: DAX snippets
docs.text: Available builders: SUM, DISTINCTCOUNT, DIVIDE-ratio, TOTALYTD, TOTALQTD, MoM, prior-YoY, running total, RANKX, ALLSELECTED baseline.

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text:
aibi diagram model.json

Paste the mermaid output into any markdown file, GitHub issue, or PR — GitHub renders erDiagram blocks natively.

docs.title: Format strings cheat sheet
docs.text: Style Format Currency $#,0.00 Percent 0.0% Thousands #,0.00

docs.title: Passing a model to aibi
docs.text: aibi summary <path> — every command on this page accepts the model as a single path argument. <path> may be one of two shapes:

docs.title: 1. A shared-schema JSON dump
docs.text:
Produced by your model tool (Power BI Desktop, Tabular Editor, or the JSON export in the Semantic Model Explorer). Top-level shape: an object with tables and optional relationships, where each entry has measures, columns, name, etc. JSON that fails a top-level shape check exits 2 with a single-line stderr reason.

aibi summary model.json
aibi audit model.json
aibi lint model.json

docs.title: 2. A TMDL folder
docs.text:
If <path> is a directory, it must follow the PBIP folder layout:

<proj>/
├── <name>.Dataset/
│   └── definition/
│       ├── tables/
│       │   ├── Sales.tmdl
│       │   ├── Customer.tmdl
│       │   └── ...
│       ├── relationships.tmdl
│       └── model.tmdl
└── ...other project files

load_model walks definition/tables/*.tmdl and definition/relationships.tmdl, parses the objects inside them, and feeds the same model dict back into every command: summary, tables, audit, lint, profile, fix, export, report, diagram.

aibi summary ./MyModel.Dataset
aibi audit ./MyModel.Dataset/definition
aibi lint ./MyModel.Dataset/definition

.pbip root, *.Dataset folder, or definition/ itself are all accepted — they end at the same TMDL entry point.

docs.title: What the loader parses
docs.text:
tables/*.tmdl:

  • table <Name> declarations and the full table body
  • column <Name> — name, dataType, sourceColumn, sourceColumn, isHidden
  • measure 'Name' = <expression> — expression (single-line and multi-line DAX delimited by triple backticks), formatString

relationships.tmdl:

  • relationship <Name> — fromColumn, toColumn, isActive, crossFilterDirection, cardinality

Everything else (hierarchies, partitions, cultures, roles, perspectives, functions, expressions, annotations) is silently skipped — the toolkit only cares about what feeds the shared model dict.

docs.title: Input format choice
docs.text:
Use the JSON dump when your model tool offers one and you want one authored file that stays versioned. Use a TMDL folder when you need changes committed in your model repository or when you want to inspect an in-flight project before exporting anything.

Both paths go through the identical downstream code — there is no other difference between JSON and TMDL input.

docs.title: Linting DAX
docs.text:
aibi lint model.json

Rules: - Prefer DIVIDE over / - Avoid IFERROR (hides real errors) - Avoid no-argument ALLSELECTED

docs.title: Rule list
docs.text: Rule Why divert-by-DIVIDE divide-by-zero errors no IFERROR hides real failures no bare ALLSELECTED() ambiguous in visuals

docs.title: Naming conventions
docs.text:
• Tables: plain plural nouns ("Orders", "Customers")
  • Columns: snake_case in source, Title Case for display
  • Measures: aggregation prefix ("Total", "Count of", "Average")

docs.title: Anti-patterns
docs.text:
• Mixing abbreviations with full words in the same table
  • Measure names that duplicate column names
  • Spaces at the start or end of any object name

docs.title: Style conversions
docs.text: to_snake_case, kebab_case, pascal_case, to_display_name — pick one convention per layer and stick to it.

docs.title: Profiling
docs.text:
aibi profile model.json

Every CALCULATE, FILTER, VAR and RETURN adds weight. Weights of 5+ are flagged as heavy candidates for analysis.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text: Weight Tier 0-2 light 3-5 medium 6+ heavy

docs.title: Listing tables
docs.text:
aibi tables prints one table name per line — useful for a quick sanity check on what the model actually contains before an audit:

$ aibi tables model.json
Sales
Customer
Product
Date

If a model has been edited outside the app, tables is the first thing to run to see what survived the round trip.

docs.title: Interpreting the output
docs.text:
• Tables come from model.get("tables"), in the raw order the dump stores them.
  • Empty tables are not listed separately by this command; aibi audit reports those separately in its table-level findings.
  • Names print exactly as they appear in the model, including any stray whitespace an app may have written. That is intentional — it makes the output a reliable check for hand-edited files.

docs.title: Common follow-ups
docs.text:
• Feed the output into a diff: aibi tables before.json > tables-before.txt — it shows exactly what disappeared in an edit.
  • Run aibi audit next for the hygiene checks, or aibi diagram to see how the tables relate.
